subject: Sequencing of MSA/DPA/Order Form — conditional milestone & billing trigger
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + sequencing ask: MSA/DPA/Order form dependencies for Veridian pilot

Hi team,

Following up after yesterday's call with Patrick and Veridian procurement — they're committed to a small pilot but procurement has flagged sequencing questions that will determine our billing start and the overall close date. I captured a draft mutual action plan (attached) but need legal and infra inputs to lock the critical path.

High-level asks:
- Can legal confirm the minimum review cycle for our standard MSA + DPA (we can accept simple redline) and whether we require customer countersignature on both before billing?
- Is it acceptable to have the Order Form executed (DocuSign) with the MSA pending final DPA sign-off if we add an express data handling addendum in the order form?
- Any gating documents procurement will insist on before PO issuance (SOC 2 evidence, data flow diagram, KMS details)?

Goal: align on a sequence that lets Veridian start the pilot in June while preserving our compliance posture and limiting exposure. Attached: Veridian_MAP_v3.pdf (proposal with milestone dates).

Proposed sequencing (initial thought):
1) Signed Order Form (billing effective date = order form effective date)
2) MSA countersigned within 5 business days (or automatic acceptance clause)
3) DPA signature tracked separately; if DPA delayed > 10 business days, restrict access to PHI-scoped datasets until DPA final

Please suggest changes and provide an estimated turnaround (in business days) for MSA and DPA review so I can set expectations with procurement.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + sequencing ask: MSA/DPA/Order form dependencies for Veridian pilot

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear summary and the MAP. Quick answers up-front and then a suggested sequencing with risk points. I've attached a redline of our standard MSA with one optional clause for "preliminary order acceptance" that allows Order Forms to go effective before the DPA is fully executed, provided the customer agrees to limited data scope until DPA is signed.

Estimated review times (our side):
- MSA: 2 business days for standard, 4–6 days if substantive commercial redlines (pricing, indemnity) appear.
- DPA: 3–7 business days depending on vendor-specific Addendum requests (we've seen vendor counsel ask for more detailed SCC language which adds time).

Suggested sequence (legal-recommended):
A) Customer signs Order Form (DocuSign) with billing effective date and a short "data-scope conditionality" clause. Order Form should reference the MSA but not require DPA signature to start billing for the pilot (we can mark the pilot dataset as "non-PHI" until DPA final).
B) MSA countersigned within 5 business days (we'll prioritize).
C) DPA executed as soon as possible; if not complete within 10 business days, implement technical restrictions on dataset scope and limit token volume.
D) If procurement requires PO before Order Form, accept PO as commercial commitment but do not ramp capacity until Order Form executed.

Dependencies / blockers to flag for procurement:
- SOC 2 Type II report (we can provide redacted copy; will need an NDA to share full evidence).
- Data flow diagram and KMS key ownership (attach KMS FAQ).
- Export controls for EU-derived data (not applicable for Veridian if US-only but flag if region expands).

I'll attach the redline: MSA_redline_LB_20270517.pdf. If everyone agrees, I can prepare the small express addendum language to append to the Order Form.

—Laura
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: MAP + sequencing ask: MSA/DPA/Order form dependencies for Veridian pilot

Patrick —

Following our convo, legal recommended a short sequencing approach that should keep your pilot on track while addressing procurement's checklist. Two quick asks to help us draft the Order Form correctly:
1) Who at Veridian will be the PO/Procurement approver (name and email) so we can align the DocuSign recipient list?
2) Does Veridian need a PO before DocuSign; if so, please share the PO timeline (expected date).

We intend to send the Order Form as a DocuSign envelope that references the MSA and includes the limited data-scope clause Laura proposed. If you sign the Order Form, billing effective date will be the Order Form effective date unless you request a different start (we're flexible to have a fixed "go-live" milestone instead).

I've attached the current OrderForm_v1.xlsx for review. When you're ready we can send the DocuSign packet: https://www.docusign.com/verify/ABC123-veridian-orderform

Thanks — if procurement is targeting the 20 May sign-date I'd like to coordinate internal acceptance so we can have the pilot environment stood up by the 1 June window.

Best,

Ben / Kimberly / Laura —

Thanks for the clear plan. Procurement confirmed they can review the DocuSign Order Form this week and aim to issue a PO the same day as signature. Approver: Sarah Chen (sarah.chen@veridian.com). We do not require the DPA to be completed before the Order Form is signed for this pilot, but procurement requires a short data-scope clause limiting datasets to de-identified test data until the DPA is final — that aligns with Laura's suggestion.

Timeline we can commit to:
- 20 May: internal signoff window (our goal to sign Order Form)
- 24 May: PO issued if any follow-ups are required
- 31 May: pilot environment readiness

Action items: please send the DocuSign packet to Sarah Chen and cc me; procurement will confirm PO details after signature. Also, to expedite our internal security review, could you provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II and a one-page KMS FAQ? We understand the NDA caveat and can sign an NDA if needed.

Looking forward — Patrick
